subject: Re: Pilot concession structuring — credits, seats, and timebox
messages:
From: Alex Conway <alex@bluecup.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot pricing request — possible extension / credit conversion

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is making good progress. We ran into two blockers in the last few days: our NLU evaluation is heavier than expected (peak inference counts) and procurement needs a clear financial playbook to approve an extension.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood convert unused pilot days into a credit bucket instead of a straight extension? That would help our finance team forecast.
- If we do a pure timebox extension, what would an incremental rate look like and do you offer any concession discounts for startups in early production?

We have a short window — hoping to decide by Friday.

Appreciate any concrete options you can share (numbers are helpful).

Best,
Alex Conway
Head of Platform
Bluecup AI

--
Attachment: pilot_results_q3.csv (CSV - referenced, not attached in thread)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Conway <alex@bluecup.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-07T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing request — possible extension / credit conversion

Alex — thanks for the context and the quick timeline. Two pragmatic options that we've used successfully:

1) Timebox extension + discounted add-on days
   - 14 extra days added to the pilot; incremental rate: $1,900/day (standard: $2,300/day) = ~17% concession
   - Add-on days billed at end of extension based on consumption; expires 30 days after extension ends

2) Credit conversion (preferred for procurement clarity)
   - Convert unused run-time to a token-credit bucket; we propose a conversion rate of 500k tokens = $5,000 (example numbers)
   - Credits are valid for 90 days and can be applied to hosted or dedicated usage during that period

I want to confirm a couple of details before we finalize: current unused runway (days) and approximate token consumption rate during your heavy evaluation runs. If you can share the top-line numbers I can run the pricing worksheet and give a specific dollar figure.

I'll also loop in Karthi and Marissa to ensure commercial alignment and check if we can tighten expiry on the credit option. Attaching a quick worksheet for transparency.

Cheers,
Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: pricing_worksheet.xlsx (XLSX - pricing model)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-07T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot pricing request — need quick alignment (Bluecup)

Team — forwarding Bluecup's ask. TL;DR: heavy evaluation runs; procurement wants predictable accounting (prefers credits); client decision by Friday.

Proposed concession playbook (baseline):
- Option A (timebox): grant 14 extra days at $1,900/day (17% concession vs list) — low bookkeeping friction for us
- Option B (credits): convert up to 400k tokens unused to a credit bucket; conversion rate 500k tokens = $5k (we can scale) with 90-day expiry — procurement-friendly

Estimate P&L impact: if they take full 14 days at concession rate, run-rate delta ~ $5.6k. If credits full redemption (400k tokens -> $4k) the realized revenue depends on usage patterns; assume 60% redeem within 90 days.

Questions for you:
- Karthi: is 90-day expiry ok from a finance/recognition standpoint or do you want shorter window?
- Marissa: approve the 17% concession band? If not, what's your upper limit for non-enterprise deals this quarter?

I'm attaching the worksheet I sent to Alex. Recommend we give both options to the customer and highlight the procurement clarity on Option B.

Thanks,
Priyom

Attachment: pricing_worksheet.xlsx (XLSX - internal copy)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-07T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot pricing request — need quick alignment (Bluecup)

Agree with the two-option approach. A couple of adjustments: 
- Make credits dollar-denominated rather than token-denominated on the customer-facing doc. Example: convert unused allocation to a $4,000 credit bucket (we can map tokens internally). Easier for procurement and accounting.
- Shorten credit expiry to 60 days to reduce long-tail liability.
- For the timebox concession, cap total concession exposure at $6,000 per pilot (so 17% is OK up to that cap). If they request more, route to RevOps + Sales Leadership.

If Marissa signs off on the cap and expiry, I'll ok the language and we can send a consolidated SOW addendum.

—Karthi
Head of Revenue Operations

Alex — thanks for waiting while we aligned internally. Two concrete, signable options below: 

Option 1 — Timebox extension (lowest friction)
- 14 additional calendar days to the existing pilot
- Add-on rate: $1,900/day (17% concession vs list)
- Concession cap: $6,000 total (we absorb up to this amount)
- Billing: invoice at end of extension based on actual days used

Option 2 — Credit bucket (procurement-friendly)
- Convert up to $4,000 in unused pilot value into a pre-paid credit bucket (we will map to tokens internally)
- Credits valid for 60 days from the date of issue
- Credits apply to any Redwood consumption (hosted or Dedicated)

Next steps:
- If you prefer Option 2 we can issue a short addendum and DocuSign link (see attached SOW v2).
- If Option 1, reply with confirmation and we will schedule the extension and invoice at the end of the period.

Attachments: Bluecup_SOW_v2.pdf, pricing_worksheet.xlsx
DocuSign: https://www.docuSign.com/p/ABCDEF123456

Happy to jump on a 15-min call if you want to walk through numbers.

Best,
Priyom Das
